item.title: Adrien Rabiot nearing AC Milan renewal
item.description: Adrien Rabiot nearing AC Milan renewal Adrien Rabiot (31) is nearing a contract extension at AC Milan, according to a report from La Gazzetta dello Sport. Rabiot is having an impressive season at AC Milan under Ruben Amorim. In 10 games in Serie A, the France international already has five goals and seven assists. His current deal with the Italian side runs until the summer of 2028, whilst there is also the option to extend for a further year. However, in light of the midfielder’s excellent form, AC Milan are looking to renew. Rabiot set for salary increase AC Milan hope to have a renewal tied up before Christmas. The club want to extend Rabiot’s deal until 2030. A renewal would also entail an increase in salary from €3.5m per year to €5m, without bonuses. A key player at club level, Rabiot also remains a regular for the France national team, despite the recent managerial change. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III plans revealed for marquee Bills game up next
item.description: Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are about to walk into their biggest game of the season, against the Buffalo Bills, and the status of Kenneth Walker is the big mystery. Thanksgiving promises to deliver this week when Patrick Mahomes’ Kansas City Chiefs take on Josh Allen’s Buffalo Bills in a marquee game. Both teams are coming off victories, but the Chiefs are missing a key piece in Kenneth Walker, who also missed practice on Monday. Jordan Schultz has revealed the plan in place for Walker in the Chiefs circle as the Bills game inches closer. Kansas City Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III plans The Chiefs were thrown a lifeline when rookie Emmett Johnson came into the side for Walker and immediately looked much more ready than expected. That has allowed the Chiefs to continue on their merry way without missing a beat, because Walker was a revelation before his injury. However, a marquee game against the Bills would be a step too big even for a surprisingly successful rookie like Johnson, so the Chiefs would have wanted Walker back in contention. Speaking on Ryan Clarke’s The Pivot podcast, Schultz revealed that that is exactly what this all has been building up to, with the reports of Walker’s injury greatly exaggerated. He said: “Kenneth Walker suffered a minor groin injury a couple of weeks ago and the Chiefs held him out against Atlanta. He probably could have played Sunday against Arizona if it were a playoff game, but the Chiefs decided to give him another week. Make no mistake, they’ve also had this game circled on the calendar. Kansas City has been saving Kenneth Walker.” This is similar to the Bills protecting Josh Allen in the game against the Dolphins by having him play a less physical game to prevent injuries. Both teams are determined to come into this game at their very best, because this could well be the Super Bowl “pre-match”. Walker is ready, and due to his absence, the Chiefs now have a capable backup in Johnson to further raise their ceiling. item.title: Augsburg boss Manuel Baum handed touchline ban for Hoffenheim clash
item.description: Augsburg boss Manuel Baum handed touchline ban for Hoffenheim clash FC Augsburg have confirmed that head coach Manuel Baum will serve a one-match touchline ban following his dismissal during Sunday's 3-1 victory over Mainz. Baum was shown a straight red card by referee Martin Petersen shortly before half-time after delaying a Mainz throw-in. The DFB's sports court has subsequently handed the 47-year-old a one-match ban for unsporting conduct, meaning he will be absent from the dugout when Augsburg travel to Hoffenheim on Sunday. The suspension comes into effect 30 minutes before kick-off and remains in place until 30 minutes after the final whistle. During this period, Baum will be prohibited from entering the dressing room, players' tunnel and technical area, as well as communicating with his players or coaching staff, either directly or indirectly. Both Baum and Augsburg have accepted the ruling, meaning the decision is final. The Fuggerstädter will be looking to build on Sunday's victory over Mainz, which brought an end to a seven-match winless run in the Bundesliga.

item.title: David Moyes raises VAR questions after Everton’s defeat to Brentford
item.description: David Moyes raises VAR questions after Everton’s defeat to Brentford David Moyes Questions James Tarkowski Red Card After Everton Collapse at Brentford Everton left west London with a 4-0 defeat, a suspension problem and a familiar debate about VAR. James Tarkowski’s dismissal in the 40th minute became the turning point, and David Moyes made it clear he was not fully convinced the challenge warranted a straight red card. Tarkowski, initially booked by Craig Pawson for his tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk, saw the decision upgraded after a review. The judgement was serious foul play, with the officials focusing on the height of the challenge and the point of contact on the shin. The explanation from the officials was direct: “After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play.” The review process was then detailed further: “VAR: ‘Point of contact is on the shin. He’s got speed and intensity. Studs are high’.” It ended with the referee’s final call: “REF: ‘After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent’s safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card – and a red card’.” IMAGO Moyes doubts force behind Tarkowski challenge Moyes did not dispute why the decision was made, though he plainly had reservations. “My first feeling was that Tarky got the ball quite comfortably,” he said. “I think you might have said, ‘Did the boy come in late on Tarky? Where do you go when you get to the ball first? “You have to follow through. But after I’ve seen it again now, and I’ve seen how high his foot was, I can see the reasons. Was there enough force? I don’t know about that.” That is the key point. Contact high on the shin, studs showing, speed in the challenge, all of that gives VAR a route to intervene. The remaining question is whether the force and danger were sufficient to move it from reckless to serious foul play. Moyes clearly is not sure. Brentford punish 10-man Everton Once Everton went down to 10 men, the contest got away from them quickly. Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice in three minutes, Vitaly Janelt added a superb long-range effort and Fabio Carvalho rounded things off late on. Everton had arrived chasing a third consecutive league win, they left having been dismantled. Moyes gave Brentford credit and did not hide from his own side’s display. “As poor as we’ve probably been, lots of credit to Brentford because they’ve done a lot of good things,” he said. “They put us under pressure, but ultimately we lost two deflected goals. Shots which took deflections and went against us.” Everton face suspension blow before Liverpool clash The practical consequence is obvious. Everton remain ninth, which still reflects a decent start in broader terms, but this was a bad night made worse by a decision that will hang around for days. The red card, the defeat and the ban all land at once. For Moyes, that is the real problem.

item.title: Troy Aikman called out for ‘belittling’ ESPN colleague live on MNF
item.description: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Troy Aikman was back in the booth for the latest instalment of ESPN’s Monday Night Football despite his controversial comments during the week. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s position with ESPN has come under a lot of scrutiny over recent months. His spot in the booth for Monday’s game in Washington was even up for debate after his midweek comments on Joe Buck. Aikman has now been called out following some of the expressions he made towards ESPN’s rules analyst Russell Yurk during a piece up in the booth. The 60-year-old’s time with ESPN is ending on a sour note, with fans growing tired of the saga with the network. Troy Aikman called out over Monday Night Football moment Over the course of the 2026 season, it has become apparent that the off-air situation surrounding Aikman’s future has seeped into the on-air product. However, reporter Mike Sando took to X on Monday evening to share his frustrations with Aikman’s handling of Yurk. ‘Belittled him. Really bad form from Aikman here. Treat people well,’ said Sando. This came after Yurk was thrown up into the booth to explain the timing situation, which saw the game between the Washington Commanders and the Cincinnati Bengals come to an end despite two seconds remaining. “That’s your moment. That was your moment, Russ,” Aikman said to Yurk as he departed the booth following his explanation. Whether many fans share the same view as Sando remains to be seen, with Aikman clearly saying it in a joking manner as he smiled and laughed. There had been some people suggesting during the week that Aikman was looking to get himself fired. His comments regarding Buck, although some may agree, were certainly out of line given his professional relationship with the commentator. However, Aikman is speaking his mind now, given ESPN has not been willing to match his contractual demands. item.title: Barberton basketball great, part of 1976 title team Mark Bodnar dies
item.description: Marty Bodnar always knew where his twin brother Mark was on the basketball court, and vice versa. Together, that brotherly intuition helped them lead Barberton — along with Carter Scott, who with the Bodnars formed one of the original Big 3s, before it was such a trend — to an undefeated record and a class AAA state championship in 1976. Marty and Mark were brothers, teammates, best friends and a major part of each other’s support system for more than six decades. Following a multi-year battle with cancer, Mark Bodnar died last week. He was 67 years old. The Bodnar twins were instrumental players during that legendary Barberton run along with Scott and coach Jack Greynolds. As juniors, they helped lead Barberton to a 26-0 record and the state title. They extended that winning streak to 51 games the next season, though it was eventually snapped in the 1977 state title game. During that championship run in 1976, Marty Bodnar hit a decisive basket in the closing moments to seal the win over Canton McKinley in the regional final. The assist, via a perfectly-placed bounce pass, came from his twin brother Mark, who knew exactly where to put it. “He just always knew where I was at,” Marty said, speaking to the Beacon Journal on Monday, Nov. 23. “He’s been assisting me for 67 years. I’m gonna miss him. It’s just a sixth sense we had. I dunno, I can’t explain it. “But he was there, back in those days, and he was assisting me in so many ways throughout my life, and I was assisting him.” In 2024, that '76 Barberton squad was inducted into the Ohio Basketball Hall of Fame . After the success in high school, both brothers went to play at Michigan. Marty still lives in the Ann Arbor area. A few years ago, he was asked by a friend to speak to a fifth-grade basketball team. It just so happened that former Michigan coach and current Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh had a son on that team. After Marty Bodnar spoke to the kids, Harbaugh walked up and asked what it was like playing with his twin brother for so long, something with which the well-known football coach has some experience due to his brother John, coach of the New York Giants, being involved at the top levels of the sport. Marty told Harbaugh that he and Mark just had a connection they couldn’t explain, and it was something they treasured. “I paused, and then I said, ‘I always knew where he was on the court, and he always knew where I was,’” Marty Bodnar said. “It was just a sixth sense. A bond that twins have.” Marty noted how appreciative the family has been to see an outpouring of messages come in from all around the country, including those with a Barberton connection. Scott, the third member of that dynamic title-winning trio, called from California to offer his condolences. It showed how close the basketball community had remained after so many years. And it showed how many people Mark had touched in a positive light. “We were just so fortunate to have a great relationship, and he was so th

Together, that brotherly intuition helped them lead Barberton — along with Carter Scott, who with the Bodnars formed one of the original Big 3s, before it was such a trend — to an undefeated record and a class AAA state championship in 1976. After the success in high school, both brothers went to play at Michigan. Marty still lives in the Ann Arbor area. A few years ago, he was asked by a friend to speak to a fifth-grade basketball team. It’s not the championships, it’s the relationships. Sports brings people together. It was a great blessing in our lives.” Ryan Lewis is a sports reporter for the Beacon Journal. He can be reached at rlewis1@gannett.com. This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: Barberton basketball great, part of 1976 title team Mark Bodnar dies

item.title: Providence survives VCU in OT as Ryan Mela delivers career-high 23
item.description: Ryan Mela tied his career high with 23 points, and Malik Mack added 19 to lead Providence to a 72-66 overtime victory over VCU on Monday, Nov. 23, at the Maui Invitational in Lahaina, Hawaii. The Friars (5-1) outscored VCU 8-2 in overtime, and Mela's offensive rebound in the extra frame helped the Friars clinch the win. "It was a big win. I felt like that sealed it a little bit," Mela said after the win. "Every time a shot goes up we've got to crash. Just doing the little things – the blue-collar stuff to win. That's pretty much it." Blake Harper scored a team-high 15 points for VCU, which attempted 28 free throws, 20 more than Providence. The Rams (3-2) shot 31.2% from the field (20 of 64). Providence committed 20 turnovers but held a 46-22 advantage in points in the paint. Head coach Bryan Hodgson said his team "got in a funk at both ends of the floor" in the second half, but was proud of his players' perseverance. "Proud of our resiliency to be honest with you. I think the biggest things for me – we did a lot of things to put ourselves in position to have to be playing an overtime game," he said. "I wasn't thrilled that was our first-round matchup. That's a darn good program with a really good roster and a great coach," Hodgson said, referring to VCU head coach Phil Martelli Jr., who had previously coached Bryant. "It says a lot about their program they were able to retain the roster that they did." VCU pulled within two points in overtime on a Torey Alston jumper, but Mela's basket gave the Friars a 70-66 lead with 30 seconds remaining. Miles Byrd added two free throws with 20 seconds left. Devin Vanterpool, Providence's leading scorer, missed his third consecutive game with a sprained shoulder. Hodgson said he hoped Vanterpool would be available, but the guard was unable to practice Sunday. Providence next takes the course on Tuesday afternoon and will play the winner of Monday's fourth game between No. 8 Arizona and Colorado State in the semifinals. VCU will face the loser. "You turn around and you play. It's quick. I think it's less than 24 hours," Hodgson said. "When you're in these tournaments you've got to fix mistakes and maybe look at some things that carry over into the next scout. But you've really got to turn the page." Providence made its first seven shots to build a 16-8 lead and went ahead 25-16 on a Mack layup with 9:10 remaining in the first half. The Friars shot 17 of 28 from the field (61%) in the first half and led 40-35 at halftime. Mela scored 15 of his 23 points in the first half. VCU took its first lead when an Ahmad Nowell 3-pointer capped a 10-2 run and gave the Rams a 46-44 advantage. A 6-0 run put the Friars ahead 56-54, but VCU regained the lead on a Brandon Jennings 3-pointer with 5:10 remaining. Arrinten Page's free throw tied the game at 64 with 32 seconds left. VCU missed two shots in the final seconds of regulation, sending the game to overtime. This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Provi
item.content:encoded: Ryan Mela tied his career high with 23 points, and Malik Mack added 19 to lead Providence to a 72-66 overtime victory over VCU on Monday, Nov. 23, at the Maui Invitational in Lahaina, Hawaii. The Friars (5-1) outscored VCU 8-2 in overtime, and Mela's offensive rebound in the extra frame helped the Friars clinch the win. "It was a big win. I felt like that sealed it a little bit," Mela said after the win. "Every time a shot goes up we've got to crash. Just doing the little things – the blue-collar stuff to win. That's pretty much it." Blake Harper scored a team-high 15 points for VCU, which attempted 28 free throws, 20 more than Providence. The Rams (3-2) shot 31.2% from the field (20 of 64). Providence committed 20 turnovers but held a 46-22 advantage in points in the paint. Head coach Bryan Hodgson said his team "got in a funk at both ends of the floor" in the second half, but was proud of his players' perseverance. "Proud of our resiliency to be honest with you. I think the biggest things for me – we did a lot of things to put ourselves in position to have to be playing an overtime game," he said. "I wasn't thrilled that was our first-round matchup. That's a darn good program with a really good roster and a great coach," Hodgson said, referring to VCU head coach Phil Martelli Jr., who had previously coached Bryant. "It says a lot about their program they were able to retain the roster that they did." VCU pulled within two points in overtime on a Torey Alston jumper, but Mela's basket gave the Friars a 70-66 lead with 30 seconds remaining. Miles Byrd added two free throws with 20 seconds left. Devin Vanterpool, Providence's leading scorer, missed his third consecutive game with a sprained shoulder. Hodgson said he hoped Vanterpool would be available, but the guard was unable to practice Sunday. Providence next takes the course on Tuesday afternoon and will play the winner of Monday's fourth game between No. 8 Arizona and Colorado State in the semifinals. VCU will face the loser. "You turn around and you play. It's quick. I think it's less than 24 hours," Hodgson said. "When you're in these tournaments you've got to fix mistakes and maybe look at some things that carry over into the next scout. But you've really got to turn the page." Providence made its first seven shots to build a 16-8 lead and went ahead 25-16 on a Mack layup with 9:10 remaining in the first half. The Friars shot 17 of 28 from the field (61%) in the first half and led 40-35 at halftime. Mela scored 15 of his 23 points in the first half. VCU took its first lead when an Ahmad Nowell 3-pointer capped a 10-2 run and gave the Rams a 46-44 advantage. A 6-0 run put the Friars ahead 56-54, but VCU regained the lead on a Brandon Jennings 3-pointer with 5:10 remaining. Arrinten Page's free throw tied the game at 64 with 32 seconds left. VCU missed two shots in the final seconds of regulation, sending the game to overtime. This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Providence survives VCU in OT as Ryan Mela delivers career-high 23

item.content:encoded: After the last international break of the year, the Premier League season resumed last weekend with Premier League Matchday 11. Premier League Matchday 11 began on Saturday, November 21, with Manchester City and Fulham drawing 1- 1. It ended on Monday with Brentford blowing away Everton 4-0 at home. After Premier League Matchday 11, Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points over second-place Brighton & Hove Albion, despite drawing 2-2 against Newcastle United. Premier League Matchday 11 showed that some teams are taking time to return to form after the break, with unexpected results. Premier League Matchday 11 also showed that some teams still have ongoing issues they need to solve quickly before their seasons go off the rails. From shocking results to major upsets, here are the biggest takeaways from Premier League Matchday 11. Three Key Takeaways From Premier League Matchday 11 1. Manchester United Is Unrepairable After Blowout Loss To Liverpool A lot happened at Manchester United during the international break as former United States men’s manager Mauricio Pochettino replaced Michael Carrick in hopes of turning around the Red Devils’ disappointing season. While their first game under Pochettino was a tough away test at Liverpool, optimism remained that he could turn things around, given his experience at Tottenham Hotspur and his success there, despite not winning a trophy. Instead, Manchester United suffered a blowout loss to Liverpool, and none of their issues under Carrick were solved, making it even more evident that this club is unrepairable as the threat of relegation continues to grow. This horror show for the Red Devils started early, as Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a last-gasp challenge on Alexander Isak, leaving them with 10 men for the rest of the game. Then, everything fell apart for Manchester United as they gave up two goals to Liverpool five minutes after the red card. After the goals, Pochettino had no choice but to switch to a back five to keep the game from getting out of hand, making his first substitution in the 22nd minute by bringing on Harry Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo. While the first half ended with Liverpool 2-0 up, Manchester United were lucky not to be down by more at half-time. The Reds had an expected goals rate of 1.67 as they dominated possession, while the Red Devils had a measly expected goals rate of 0.14, as Pochettino kept going to his bench for a spark. Still, nothing was working for his team as Liverpool continued to dominate before finally breaking through with two more goals, and the game ended with Liverpool running out 4-0 victors over Manchester United. Now, after Premier League Matchday 11, the Red Devils are 19th in the Premier League table with eight points, one point above last-place Crystal Palace. Pochettino’s tenure with the Red Devils got off to the worst start possible as they gave up four goals for the second consecutive game while being dominated by their rival from start to finish. Manchester United finished the game with an expected goals rate of 0.63 and three shots on target, while Liverpool had an expected goals rate of 4.38 and 11 shots on target, with 64% possession. Everyone except Bruno Fernandes failed to make an impact, as no one else had a shot on target. The situation at Manchester United keeps getting worse, regardless of who the manager is. The team continues to make careless mistakes; the defence can’t shut down opponents, the offence struggles to create chances, and Bruno Fernandes has struggled this season after his best season as a Red Devil last year. We will learn more about this team this week in the UEFA Champions League. Still, it’s starting to look like Manchester United’s problems are unrepairable as the threat of relegation continues to loom, and it may take a while for the Red Devils to find any momentum in the Premier League this season. 2. Manchester City In Trouble After Unexpected Draw Against Fulham Before the international break, Manchester City were in the middle of a major skid, suffering three consecutive defeats after winning their first seven games of the season. As a result, they dropped from first place to third. However, the Cityzens had a great opportunity to end their woes after the international break, facing a lowly Fulham side at home in Premier League Matchday 11. Instead, they failed to win for the fourth consecutive game, with the Fulham vs Manchester City game ending in a 1-1 draw. A theme for the Cityzens during this winless streak has been their inability to get off to fast starts. It became apparent in Premier League Matchday 11 as Manchester City gave up a goal to Fulham 16 minutes into the game. After the goal, it looked like the Cityzens were back on track when Erling Haaland scored the game-tying goal in the 24th minute. However, VAR later controversially disallowed it due to a foul Haaland committed on Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. Manchester City continued to create chances in the first half but failed to be clinical, going into half-time down one goal. They finished the first half with an expected goals rate of 1.63 as Haaland uncharacteristically missed clear chances, and they could’ve easily gone down two goals if not for a great save by Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 44th minute. In the second half, the Cityzens came out with urgency, dominating possession in hopes of an equaliser. They were rewarded in the 57th minute when Elliot Anderson scored his first goal of the season with a beautiful volley. Eight minutes later, Anderson almost scored his second on another volley, but it went wide, and that was Manchester City’s last real chance to take the lead. In the end, the Cityzens finished with a 1.88 expected goals rate and three shots on target, with 0.25 coming in the second half, as they failed to threaten Fulham’s defence after Anderson’s goal. Even though Manchester City had the higher expected goals rate, Fulham were the better team, with four shots on target and looking like the team most likely to score a second goal. Fulham got a well-deserved point despite being outpossessed, but this result speaks more about the Cityzens’ form. They have now failed to beat three teams below the top 10, and Haaland has gone scoreless for three straight games. Things won’t get easier for Manchester City after Premier League Matchday 11, as they face a brutal four-game stretch against top-10 opposition. The Cityzens missed a golden opportunity to get back on track in Premier League Matchday 11 ahead of this stretch, and now, after this draw, they face a huge risk of falling further down the table, starting this week against Arsenal. item.title: Como plot shock transfer move for Man Utd outcast Joshua Zirkzee after Moise Kean injury disaster
item.description: Chelsea FC v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Como have emerged as potential suitors for out-of-favour Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee ahead of the January transfer window. Cesc Fabregas' side are exploring attacking options after summer signing Moise Kean suffered a major injury setback that will sideline the Italy international for several more months. Como eye Zirkzee after Moise Kean injury blow Como have joined a growing list of Serie A clubs interested in signing Zirkzee during the January transfer window. According to Gianluca Di Marzio , the Italian side are weighing up attacking reinforcements following a major injury setback to Kean. Fabregas confirmed over the weekend that Kean faces another lengthy spell on the sidelines after aggravating an issue in training last week. The Como manager stated that the striker will be out for "another few months, not weeks", forcing the club to reassess their forward options. Recurring tibia issue sidelines Kean for months Kean has battled a recurring tibia problem for several months, an issue that predates his move to Como. Despite playing through pain earlier in the campaign, the 26-year-old has endured repeated setbacks and has not featured since representing Italy during the September-October international break. Just as he neared a return to full training, Kean suffered another fitness relapse that may now require surgical intervention. With the forward ruled out for the foreseeable future, Como are "exploring their options" in the market, though no formal negotiations have opened with Manchester United. Zirkzee struggles for minutes at Old Trafford A return to Italy could offer a lifeline to Zirkzee, who has endured a frustrating spell since arriving at Old Trafford from Bologna for an initial €42.5m in 2024. The Netherlands international has fallen down the pecking order and is yet to start a single competitive fixture for United during the 2026-27 season. Zirkzee has accumulated just 231 minutes of action across 11 substitute appearances in the Premier League, Champions League and EFL Cup. While he appeared surplus to requirements under former boss Michael Carrick, his future under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino remains uncertain. Serie A rivals monitor United forward Como are far from the only Italian club tracking Zirkzee's availability ahead of the winter window. Napoli are also reportedly keeping tabs on the Dutchman as they prepare to enter the market for a striker should Lorenzo Lucca depart the club. Zirkzee's proven track record in Serie A ensures he remains a sought-after target across the division. Alongside interest from Como and Napoli, the forward has previously been linked with moves to Juventus, Roma and Milan during his difficult stint in England.

item.title: Inter Milan Legend Tips Noslin for Netherlands Role: ”Alternative to Summerville”
item.description: Inter Milan Legend Tips Noslin for Netherlands Role: ”Alternative to Summerville” Former Inter Milan midfielder Wesley Sneijder firmly believes Tijjani Noslin is worthy of a call-up from the Netherlands. Tijjani Noslin Struggled At the Start of His Career The 27-year-old has now established himself as a key player at Lazio, but his path was filled with hurdles, rejections and disappointments. The Amsterdam native is a childhood Ajax supporter, but a registration issue denied him the chance to join the club’s famous academy. Tijjani Noslin (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) The attacker was also dropped by Twente, and in his early twenties, he had to work in food delivery to support himself while playing in the country’s lower divisions. In 2020, he joined DHSC, an amateur club in Utrecht, but it turned out to be a blessing in disguise, as it allowed him the opportunity to meet Sneijder, who was associated with the club. Wesley Sneijder’s Role The 2010 World Cup finalist realised Noslin was too good for this level, so in 2021, he helped him secure a move to Fortuna Sittard. In January 2024, the striker joined Hellas Verona, playing an instrumental role in their Serie A survival bid, before following Marco Baroni to Lazio the following summer. Noslin’s Rise to Prominence at Lazio Noslin was considered a mere squad player in his first two seasons in the Italian capital, but under Gennaro Gattuso, he became the club’s main striker, while also filling in on the wings when required. He currently leads the club’s scoring charts with six goals in 12 Serie A appearances. Sneijder on Noslin’s Early Career Hardships After his Man of the Match performance against Lecce , Noslin received praise from his longtime mentor Sneijder. Speaking on the Dutch podcast Wes & Raf (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), the retired midfielder recalled the striker’s early days. Before he joined DHSC, everyone considered him a very difficult lad. He was a good player, but very complicated, never punctual… So I sat down and spoke with him, and we agreed on some arrangements. After just a few training sessions, I realised that he had everything required to become a professional footballer. He had enormous potential. We started working together, and I told him: ‘Don’t mess me around; if you don’t, I’ll take you to the Eredivisie’. He said it was impossible, but I managed to do it. Within two years, I had genuinely taken him to the Dutch league. Now he plays for Lazio and is one of their most important players. I kept my promise, that’s a fact. Sneijder Wants Noslin With The Netherlands Sneijder also invited Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez to consider adding the Lazio man to the Dutch national team. If he continues like this, why shouldn’t he receive a call-up from the Netherlands? Trust me, he is an excellent alternative to Summerville. Recent reports from the Netherlands claimed that the Surinamese national team will try to convince him to join, alongside his Lazio teammate, Danilho Doekhi, who is also uncapped.

item.title: SEC Championship Game: Paths for Alabama, Texas or Tennessee to play Georgia
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - DECEMBER 06: A view of the SEC Championship logo on the field prior to the 2025 SEC Championship between the Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on December 06, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) Todd Kirkland The 2026 SEC Championship Game will make history as the conference’s final championship game before the College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams in 2027. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] No. 1 Georgia already punched its ticket after its win on Saturday. It will be the program’s sixth straight appearance in the championship game. But the Bulldogs are still waiting to learn their opponent with three teams in the running: No. 3 Alabama, No. 5 Texas and No. 9 Tennessee. Here’s what each team needs to happen to advance. ALABAMA MAKES SEC CHAMPIONSHIP GAME IF... There are two paths for the Crimson Tide. Alabama beats Auburn plus Texas loses to Texas A&M and Tennessee loses to Vanderbilt OR Alabama beats Auburn plus wins from Tennessee, LSU and Mississippi State In the second scenario, Alabama would hold the conference opponent win percentage tiebreaker, despite its loss to Tennessee. Georgia defeated Alabama back in September for its first win in Tuscaloosa since 2007. The two sides have met in the SEC Championship Game five times. TEXAS MAKES SEC CHAMPIONSHIP GAME IF... There are three paths for the Longhorns. Texas beats Texas A&M and Alabama loses to Auburn OR Texas beats Texas A&M and Tennessee loses to Vanderbilt OR Texas beats Texas A&M and either Mississippi State or LSU lose No matter the path, Texas has to beat Texas A&M on Friday night or it will miss out on the SEC Championship Game. And their playoff fate will be left to the College Football Playoff committee. Georgia and Texas met in the 2024 SEC Championship Game with the Bulldogs winning in overtime. TENNESSEE MAKES SEC CHAMPIONSHIP GAME IF... For the Vols, there is only one path to make it to the SEC Championship Game. Tennessee needs Texas A&M to beat Texas on Friday night and the Vols must beat Vanderbilt. Georgia and Tennessee did not play this season after the SEC conference schedule moved to 10 games. It’s the first time since 1991 that the Bulldogs and Vols haven’t met in a season. The two programs have never faced each other in the SEC Championship Game. WHEN IS THE SEC CHAMPIONSHIP GAME? The SEC Championship Game is set for Saturday, Dec. 5 with a 4 p.m. kickoff at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The game will air on Channel 2. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Where to watch Big Ten volleyball tournament: Full TV schedule, channel, live streams, scores, bracket for 2026
item.description: Where to watch Big Ten volleyball tournament: Full TV schedule, channel, live streams, scores, bracket for 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . College volleyball fans, rejoice — the Big Ten is hosting their inaugural conference tournament this weekend in Fishers, Indiana. As one of college volleyball's most elite conferences, this tournament is long overdue. Competition has been fierce this season, with several programs showing promise to make national campaigns come December. 15 of the conference's 18 teams qualified for the inaugural tournament, with Iowa, Northwestern and Ohio State ruled out of contention. As expected, Nebraska clinched the No. 1 overall seed, earning themselves a double-bye alongside Oregon, Penn State and Wisconsin. The Huskers already clinched the regular-season title with an impressive 28-0 record. Who will conquer the first-ever Big Ten volleyball tournament? Here's everything you need to know about the competition, including TV channel and streaming options for each match. Where to watch Big Ten volleyball tournament TV channel : Big Ten Network, Fox, FS2 Live stream : Fubo , B1G+ Each match in the inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament will be broadcast live on Big Ten Network. Cord-cutters can also catch the action on B1G+, or Fubo , which offers a free trial for all new users. Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) item.title: ‘Every night’ – Luka Doncic’s latest LA Lakers antics have left NBA fans ‘exhausted’
item.description: Photo by Ryan Sirius Sun/Getty Images Despite being one of the best players in the league, Luka Doncic can sometimes be a divisive figure in the league because of the way he approaches defenders. In particular, it is Doncic’s ability and constant efforts to draw fouls that frustrate a large portion of the fanbase, as they believe he focuses too much on getting to the free-throw line. For a player of Doncic’s offensive calibre, the fixation on trying to draw fouls does tend to hold his game back on occasion, with one example during the LA Lakers’ win over the Utah Jazz proving to be the perfect example. Luka Doncic’s eight-second violation while trying to draw a foul draws negative reactions from fans In the early stages of the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Utah Jazz, Luka Doncic was bringing the ball up when he found himself being picked up full-court by his former Dallas Mavericks teammate Josh Green. In an effort to draw a foul before crossing the half-court line, Doncic would end up with an eight-second violation, having not brought the ball up within eight seconds of the shot clock starting after collecting the inbound pass. Understandably, such a rookie mistake from a veteran like Doncic proved to be frustrating, especially considering many fans saw this as a blatant attempt to draw a foul rather than get a good look on the offensive end. One fan wrote: “Every night it’s something else from him. Just a whiny-a** b****. Exhausted by all of it, y’all.” Another fan added: “Watching Luka is infuriating. He’s so good; just play the f****** game you’re paid millions of dollars to play! $200/ticket to watch this? I want my money back, Adam Silver!” A third fan even observed Doncic’s extra effort to draw a foul: “Dude was loading up that head whiplash for the whistle!” A fourth fan even went as far as to say that the Dallas Mavericks were right to trade Luka Doncic: “Nico was right, man; f****** trash player!” Focusing on his performance on the night, a fifth fan called out Doncic’s woes on the offensive end: “Another inefficient night vs. one of the worst defensive teams in the league.” And lastly, one final fan claimed this reaction from Doncic was a sign of his irritation with the Lakers: “Is it me or does it seem like Luka is unhappy? He seems extremely frustrated every game!” Doncic had a remarkably poor night against the Jazz, scoring 28 points on 8/24 shooting from the field and 3/14 shooting from beyond the arc. While he did dish out eight assists, Doncic’s four personal fouls in the first half got him in trouble, and forced the Lakers to play a large portion of the second half without him, so as to not lose him later in the game. item.title: Major setback awaits JJ Gabriel at Real Madrid after highly publicised Man United exit
item.description: Major setback awaits JJ Gabriel at Real Madrid after highly publicised Man United exit JJ Gabriel is reportedly set for an immediate setback at Real Madrid following his highly controversial Manchester United exit. Acrimonious departure A week ago, Gabriel confirmed his United exit via social media, putting an end to weeks of speculation over his future. In September, he and his representatives stunned United by officially requesting the club to cancel his registration. He subsequently withdrew from training at Carrington, choosing instead to follow his own individual programme in Spain. United’s attempts to persuade him to stay went unanswered by the player’s camp. A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that United found out about Gabriel’s exit via his social media announcement. United may still hold the teenager’s registration until the season’s end, but it will not stop him from moving to a European Union club; he now possesses an EU passport through his mother, who is of Cypriot heritage. It’s understood that Gabriel has a verbal agreement to join Madrid . The move is expected to go through at the turn of the year. However, according to the Manchester Evening News , the teenager faces an immediate problem once he signs on the dotted line. Gabriel put in his place According to the newspaper, Gabriel is set to begin his career at Real Madrid in a low-key fashion, with the Spanish giants guided by their prior experience of having Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard. Neither Castilla, Real Madrid’s B team, nor the C team may sign players before January. Source: API-Football, Transfermarkt, Wikipedia Gabriel is expected to play for the Under-18s in the interim, but upon joining Madrid he will not initially train with the first team. It could be a blow to him and his father, one of whose stated grievances for leaving United was wanting greater involvement with the senior squad. Madrid’s plan is for Gabriel to train and play for the B team. It’s understood that Madrid are eager not to repeat the mistakes they made with Odegaard a decade ago. Having been signed at the age of 15, Odegaard was rushed into the first team but struggled to secure playing time under Carlo Ancelotti and Zinedine Zidane, making it eventually necessary for him to depart the Santiago Bernabeu to preserve his career. Journalist Guillem Balague told the BBC that Madrid are also not happy with the media circus surrounding Gabriel’s switch from Old Trafford. “Madrid learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.” “Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded.” “Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. Acrimonious departure A week ago, Gabriel confirmed his United exit via social media, putting an end to weeks of speculation over his future. In September, he and his representatives stunned United by officially requesting the club to cancel his registration. He subsequently withdrew from training at Carrington, choosing instead to follow his own individual programme in Spain. United’s attempts to persuade him to stay went unanswered by the player’s camp. A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that United found out about Gabriel’s exit via his social media announcement. United may still hold the teenager’s registration until the season’s end, but it will not stop him from moving to a European Union club; he now possesses an EU passport through his mother, who is of Cypriot heritage. It’s understood that Gabriel has a verbal agreement to join Madrid . The move is expected to go through at the turn of the year. However, according to the Manchester Evening News , the teenager faces an immediate problem once he signs on the dotted line. Gabriel put in his place According to the newspaper, Gabriel is set to begin his career at Real Madrid in a low-key fashion, with the Spanish giants guided by their prior experience of having Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard. Neither Castilla, Real Madrid’s B team, nor the C team may sign players before January. Source: API-Football, Transfermarkt, Wikipedia Gabriel is expected to play for the Under-18s in the interim, but upon joining Madrid he will not initially train with the first team. It could be a blow to him and his father, one of whose stated grievances for leaving United was wanting greater involvement with the senior squad. Madrid’s plan is for Gabriel to train and play for the B team. It’s understood that Madrid are eager not to repeat the mistakes they made with Odegaard a decade ago. Having been signed at the age of 15, Odegaard was rushed into the first team but struggled to secure playing time under Carlo Ancelotti and Zinedine Zidane, making it eventually necessary for him to depart the Santiago Bernabeu to preserve his career. Journalist Guillem Balague told the BBC that Madrid are also not happy with the media circus surrounding Gabriel’s switch from Old Trafford. “Madrid learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.” “Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded.” “Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. At Real Madrid, nobody is bigger than the club. The idea was to keep everything quiet until January and announce it then. But with Gabriel already training in Madrid, the secret was never going to last.” United are next in action on Wednesday when they face Sporting CP in the Champions League.

item.title: RB Leipzig and PreZero extend partnership until 2029
item.description: RB Leipzig and PreZero extend partnership until 2029 RB Leipzig and PreZero have extended their partnership, which began in 2022, by a further three years until 30th June 2029 . The Neckarsulm-based company will remain an Official Supplier of the Red Bulls and continue to advise the club on matters relating to the circular economy. The two partners share a common goal: to use resources responsibly, keep materials in circulation and develop innovative ideas within football. Putting the circular economy into practice – from stadium seats to Zero Waste Two projects in particular highlight what the partnership has achieved so far: In May 2024, the Red Bull Arena’s waste and recycling management system was certified by TÜV Süd in line with DIN SPEC 91436 “Zero Waste” at Bronze maturity level. At the time, more than 85% of waste generated on the stadium grounds was already being recycled or undergoing other forms of material recovery. This rate had more than doubled since 2019. The old blue stadium seats from the Red Bull Arena have also been given a second life. As part of the “SEATainability” project, they were recycled into Soccercourt boards. Seats that once accommodated fans now serve a new purpose on a football pitch. Stephan Czieplik, Chief Revenue Officer at RB Leipzig: “We’ve achieved a great deal together with PreZero since 2022. The Zero Waste certification of our Red Bull Arena and projects such as SEATainability demonstrate what’s possible through our partnership. We want to continue developing new ideas that conserve resources while delivering tangible benefits for our club.” Discover more Fixtures Red Bull Arena Men's first team Tickets Fan Zone

item.title: See which Mount Union football players made the 2026 All-OAC team
item.description: Ten Mount Union players have been named to the 2026 All-Ohio Athletic Conference Football Team. Quarterback Mikey Maloney received first-team honors for the second straight season. He led the OAC in passing yards with 2,846 and total offense at 333.5 yards a game. Both totals ranked eighth in the nation. Receiver Mason Ashby , defensive back Rickie Williams and offensive linemen Mitch Coffee and Patrick Lavelle were also named to the first team. Ashby led the OAC with an average of 100.2 yards a game. He was the only receiver in the conference to average more than 100 yards a game. Williams led the Mount Union secondary with 57 tackles, including a team-high 41 solos. Coffee and Lavelle helped block for a Purple Raiders offense that led the OAC in total offense at 516.8 yards a game which ranked fifth in the nation. Offensive lineman Fred Fevier, defensive back Dallas Richardson and receiver Brayden Harris were Mount Union's selections on the second team. Defensive linemen Jackson Harris and Gabe Gannelli were named honorable mention. This article originally appeared on The Repository: See which Mount Union football players made the 2026 All-OAC team

item.title: The Blue Jays’ reported offer for Tarik Skubal revealed after his $450 million Mets deal
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Tarik Skubal has signed the largest pitching contract in MLB history with the New York Mets, but the Toronto Blue Jays put a pretty large offer on the table themselves. After a brief stint with the Los Angeles Dodgers, Tarik Skubal will now play for the New York Mets starting next season. The two-time Cy Young Award winner signed a deal worth $450 million over nine years with the franchise, comfortably surpassing Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s massive deal with his former team. Skubal has had many suitors since it became evident that he would be leaving the Detroit Tigers last year. The Dodgers got him in a trade, but it soon became clear that other teams were waiting to pounce on the pitcher in free agency. And now, the Blue Jays’ reported offer to Skubal has been revealed. The Toronto Blue Jays reportedly gave Tarik Skubal a $420 million contract offer Toronto had been among the teams competing for his signature, alongside the Mets, Dodgers and San Diego Padres. If reports are to be believed, the Dodgers never made a formal offer, and the Mets came out as the eventual winners in the sweepstakes. Toronto’s offer was reported by the New York Post’s Jon Heyman, with The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon also reporting that the Blue Jays had put more than $400 million on the table. “The Toronto Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal $420M but the Mets topped it with $450M to seal the deal with the two-time Cy Young award winner,” the report reads. New York’s offer also reportedly includes a $45 million signing bonus and full no-trade protection, which may have tipped the scales further in their favour. The size of the contract means there will be significant pressure on Skubal moving forward. The pitcher will have to deliver for a Mets team that has so far significantly underperformed their massive payroll. As for the Blue Jays, this marks yet another failed pursuit for a big superstar. item.title: How to watch Champions League: Live streams, TV channels and latest fixtures for 2026/27 season schedule
item.description: How to watch Champions League: Live streams, TV channels and latest fixtures for 2026/27 season schedule originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The return of the UEFA Champions League has fans anticipating a thrilling competition from start to finish, as the most prestigious knockout soccer tournament in the world soldiers on seeking to crown a new champion for the 2026/27 season. Two-time defending title-holders Paris Saint-Germain are now looking to become just the third club ever to win three consecutive European championships. They will look to hold off last year's finalists Arsenal as well as fellow Premier League giants Man City and Liverpool . Other top contenders include Real Madrid helmed by Champions League icon Jose Mourinho, their Clasico rivals Barcelona , German giants Bayern Munich, and many other massive European brands. All roads lead to the final on June 5, 2027 at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The Sporting News looks at the key fixture details and how to follow the matches. Champions League live streams, TV channels in USA Every single match of the Champions League matches for the 2026/27 season will be streamed on Paramount+ in the United States, as CBS holds the broadcast rights in the United States through the 2029/30 season. Paramount+ combines the best content from the worlds of sports, news and entertainment, including the NFL, UFC, March Madness, UEFA Champions League and more. You can stream live events as well as thousands of hours of shows and movies. Some Champions League games are broadcast each matchweek by the network, either on CBS, or CBS Sports Network. Matches televised on either channel can be accessed on Fubo in the United States. Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) Other matches will occasionally be streamed live on CBS Sports Golazo Network, a free-to-air digital streaming platform. item.title: Aljamain Sterling Raises Questions Over Scoring After UFC Qatar Loss to Kevin Vallejos
item.description: Aljamain Sterling at UFC 300 | Photo: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Aljamain Sterling’s move to featherweight has had its ups and downs, starting with a dominant win over Calvin Kattar, then a razor-close decision loss to Mosvar Evloev. He then bounced back with wins over Brian Ortega and Youssef Zalal, and just had a very close fight with 24-year-old contender Kevin Vallejos. At UFC Qatar , Sterling and Vallejos stifled each other’s best abilities, leading to a very contested fight round after round. The matchup between Sterling and Vallejos was extremely technical. The former bantamweight champion struggled to work in grappling and find openings, while Vallejos struggled to employ his game plan of keeping pressure and finding the knockout shot. The scorecards favored Vallejos’ action, with two judges giving him the win 30-27 and one 29-28. What does Aljamain Sterling think of the scoring in his UFC Qatar fight? Reflecting on the matchup during The Ariel Helwani Show , Aljamain Sterling said, “I’m not calling it a robbery. I just wish we could get some explanation on what they’re actually scoring.” Sterling went into detail on his questions about scoring criteria: “I know the criteria is damage, but what is damage when you’re being outstruck, and what’s damage when a guy is swinging and missing and not landing anything of significance.” Aljamain Sterling proposes a change to how fights are judged: “When the scorecards came, I thought it was going to go my way, and then when it didn’t, I was in disbelief. I was baffled. I don’t know what we’re scoring. I don’t know what scores anymore. I still think judges should be in the back room watching the fights. Why not? If you wanna progress the sport, you can’t keep changing the rules from week to week, where one thing happens, you score it this way, and then the next week you see something else scored a different way.” — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 23, 2026 Sterling went on to give Vallejos a lot of credit, calling him the most dangerous 145-pounder. Vallejos has been on a tear in his recent fights, securing knockouts and Performance of the Night bonuses against both Giga Chikadze and Josh Emmett. Vallejos is a Contender Series alumni and his only loss of his career came against Jean Silva in their Contender Series matchup back in 2023. ALSO READ: What’s Next for Navajo Stirling After Knocking Out Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar? However, Sterling was able to stay at distance and did not take too many clean shots, so he does have valid questions about the scoring criteria, especially since he did narrowly outstrike the young contender in the first two rounds, went 1-14 on takedowns, and had 3:32 seconds of control time throughout the fight. While Vallejos did keep pressure on and had arguably the cleaner, more damaging strikes, Sterling still did great defensively and had the striking numbers. Ajlamain Sterling explains why he should ha
item.content:encoded: Aljamain Sterling at UFC 300 | Photo: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Aljamain Sterling’s move to featherweight has had its ups and downs, starting with a dominant win over Calvin Kattar, then a razor-close decision loss to Mosvar Evloev. He then bounced back with wins over Brian Ortega and Youssef Zalal, and just had a very close fight with 24-year-old contender Kevin Vallejos. At UFC Qatar , Sterling and Vallejos stifled each other’s best abilities, leading to a very contested fight round after round. The matchup between Sterling and Vallejos was extremely technical. The former bantamweight champion struggled to work in grappling and find openings, while Vallejos struggled to employ his game plan of keeping pressure and finding the knockout shot. The scorecards favored Vallejos’ action, with two judges giving him the win 30-27 and one 29-28. What does Aljamain Sterling think of the scoring in his UFC Qatar fight? Reflecting on the matchup during The Ariel Helwani Show , Aljamain Sterling said, “I’m not calling it a robbery. I just wish we could get some explanation on what they’re actually scoring.” Sterling went into detail on his questions about scoring criteria: “I know the criteria is damage, but what is damage when you’re being outstruck, and what’s damage when a guy is swinging and missing and not landing anything of significance.” Aljamain Sterling proposes a change to how fights are judged: “When the scorecards came, I thought it was going to go my way, and then when it didn’t, I was in disbelief. I was baffled. I don’t know what we’re scoring. I don’t know what scores anymore. I still think judges should be in the back room watching the fights. Why not? If you wanna progress the sport, you can’t keep changing the rules from week to week, where one thing happens, you score it this way, and then the next week you see something else scored a different way.” — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 23, 2026 Sterling went on to give Vallejos a lot of credit, calling him the most dangerous 145-pounder. Vallejos has been on a tear in his recent fights, securing knockouts and Performance of the Night bonuses against both Giga Chikadze and Josh Emmett. Vallejos is a Contender Series alumni and his only loss of his career came against Jean Silva in their Contender Series matchup back in 2023. ALSO READ: What’s Next for Navajo Stirling After Knocking Out Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar? However, Sterling was able to stay at distance and did not take too many clean shots, so he does have valid questions about the scoring criteria, especially since he did narrowly outstrike the young contender in the first two rounds, went 1-14 on takedowns, and had 3:32 seconds of control time throughout the fight. While Vallejos did keep pressure on and had arguably the cleaner, more damaging strikes, Sterling still did great defensively and had the striking numbers. Ajlamain Sterling explains why he should have won his UFC Qatar fight Sterling explained his fighting style and how he viewed the matchup. He said, “I’m not the most powerful puncher. I can be honest with that, but I do know I can hit a lot of volume, I can make you work, and I can outpace you, and look for the finish that way. I think styles like mine almost get penalized, because we’re not that one hitter quitter type of fighter, and not looking to swing haymakers the whole time in a barnfight.” The former UFC champion added, “So I feel like that should have been enough to get the job done. Just based on the criteria, every single round I outstruck him, even off my back I outstruck him, and somehow I still managed to come up short.” Sterling also explained why he believes fighters should receive more detailed explanations of judging decisions. According to him, understanding what swayed the judges would help competitors adjust their game plans and focus on the factors that matter most when scoring rounds. Such a change could give fighters greater clarity on how to approach future matchups. However, the Unified Rules of MMA, developed with contributions from legendary referee “Big John” McCarthy , already outline the scoring criteria used by judges. For now, there appears to be little indication that the system will change in the way Sterling is proposing. Nevertheless, MMA continues to evolve, leaving room for potential changes in the future. Game planning remains crucial in high-stakes matchups, where both fighters bring significant strengths and a single mistake can prove costly. While Sterling would welcome greater transparency from judges, he has consistently demonstrated an ability to prepare effectively for opponents. His technical approach, high-volume striking, and ability to dictate the pace have helped him win rounds and find success against some of the toughest competition in the sport. item.title: Where to watch Davis Cup Finals 2026: Full schedule, TV channel, live stream and prize money
item.description: Where to watch Davis Cup Finals 2026: Full schedule, TV channel, live stream and prize money originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After 11 months of international competition, the Davis Cup is officially down to the Final 8. One more week of matchups will determine the tournament's 2026 champions. Often referred to as the 'World Cup of Tennis', the Davis Cup features men's teams from across 150 countries, creating the largest annual team competition in the sport. The Cup began in 1900 as a singular match between the United States and Great Britain, and has since evolved into an international affair each year. The Final 8 is set to take place in Bologna, Italy this week, using a single-day, best-of-three knockout format. Three-time defending champions Italy will be chasing a fourth consecutive title, but without star Jannik Sinner. Carlos Alcaraz will be leading Spain's team, while Alexander Zverev represents Germany. Which nation will lift the Davis Cup trophy? Here's everything you need to know about the Davis Cup Finals, including TV channel and streaming options for the international men's tournament. Where to watch Davis Cup Finals 2026: TV channel, live stream TV channel: Tennis Channel Live stream: Fubo The 2026 Davis Cup Finals will be broadcast live on the Tennis Channel in the United States. Fans can also stream the action live on Fubo , which offers a FREE trial. Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) When is Davis Cup Finals 2026? item.title: Rob Gronkowski is ‘a little worried’ about the Jacksonville Jaguars after what he’s noticed
item.description: Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images Rob Gronkowski has suggested that the Jacksonville Jaguars are starting to make him a ‘little worried’ due to their inconsistency, which he thinks was on display against the New York Giants in Week 11. The Jaguars managed just 18 points against the Giants, their lowest points total since mid-September when they were beaten 20-13 by the Denver Broncos. Despite the recent 23-18 loss to the Giants, the Jags are still comfortably top of the AFC South and look pretty nailed on for a playoff berth. However, Gronkowski is worried that Jacksonville use up all their ‘greatness’ in the regular season and then struggle in the playoffs. Rob Gronkowski suggests Jaguars are too inconsistent during playoffs Speaking to NFL on Fox , he said: “I am a little worried about the Jags because of their inconsistency. They kind of showed and displayed this last year. Yeah, they’ve got a great team and they can show greatness at times, but then they hit the playoffs, the last couple of years, and boom, they just unload in a terrible way. It’s like they unload all their greatness.” Talking specifically about the Week 11 loss, he added: “It’s like they’ve used it all up throughout the whole season, and now they’re already showing periods like this game and moments where they’re just not showing up. They’ve got to show up on a consistent basis. “It’s not like, ‘Hey, you know, the playoffs are kicking in. We’re going to dominate now. We’re going to play our best football’. You’ve got to continue to play your best football throughout the whole year, especially against solid opponents. “Like the New York Giants. Yes, they shocked everyone, but they’re a solid team. Harbaugh is a great coach, you know? They’ve got McCarthy now. They’re playing together as a team. They want to win. It’s like there are no individuals. “Everyone’s in it together with the New York Giants. I’m not saying the Jags aren’t. I mean, I feel like there aren’t any individuals on that team, but they’re just too inconsistent over the years.” The Jaguars made it to the Wild Card Playoffs in 2025, losing 27-24 against the Buffalo Bills and you could make a case that their inconsistency was on display then. Trevor Lawrence is one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL but against the Bills, he threw a game-losing interception in the final few minutes, which cost his side. Prior to that, they competed in the 2022/23 season playoffs and were bested by the Kansas City Chiefs when Nick Bolton and Jaylen Watson capitalised on fumbles and interceptions in the fourth quarter to help their team win 27-20. It does feel like the Jaguars are never really blown away when they are beaten in the postseason. Instead, individual errors or lapses in concentration seem to be what costs them. But it’s hard to predict if that will change in 2026/27, as apart from the Giants’ loss, they have looked like one of the most complete teams in the regular campaign. item.title: Buffalo Bills did something ‘incredible’ with Josh Allen to ‘unleash’ him against the Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images The Thanksgiving game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills is the marquee fixture, and the latter have done something ‘incredible’ with Josh Allen to prepare him for it. When the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, it will be a clash between two marquee quarterbacks and two winning teams. Patrick Mahomes is not surrendering his position and Josh Allen is coming for it, while this could easily be the Super Bowl game this season. To prepare Allen for this game in the best possible way, the Bills did something ‘incredible’ during their recent game against the Dolphins. Josh Allen protected against the Dolphins The Bills faced no issues dispatching the Dolphins in their recent game to go 9-1 this season and cement themselves as the best team in the NFL. Allen managed to gain 304 yards with his passing, completing 27/45 attempts, but it was a sloppy game by his usually world-class standards. NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, speaking on Ryan Clarke’s The Pivot podcast, said that Allen’s game was by design, as the Bills prioritised protecting him at all costs. Schultz said that for the first time ever, Allen took no part in any rushes, design runs, or scrambles, and that was all intentional. He said: “Something happened Sunday against Miami. And I’m looking at it right now. This is pretty incredible because I want to make sure I get this right. Josh Allen, this is the first time we’ve ever seen this in his career. He finished the game with zero rushing attempts. “No design runs, no scrambles, nothing. Everything went through the passing game or the running backs. And my understanding is that this was very strictly and deliberately by design. Buffalo wanted to make sure that Josh was fresh for Thursday, when the entire playbook will be available and he’ll be fully unleashed.” It is no surprise to see the Bills preparing this way for a game that could go a long way towards solidifying their championship prospects and placing Allen as the MVP favourite. Allen is now well-rested and safe to play to his full strengths in a game that will be watched and analysed by millions, and the Bills’ gamble will be spoken about as genius if they win that game after winning against the Dolphins as well. item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following home loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers played host to the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday night looking to keep things moving in the right direction. Unfortunately, a lack of size and 3-point production did them in as the Sixers fell to the Blazers 128-111 to fall to 14-4 on the season. LeBron James had 23 points, six rebounds, and three assists for Philadelphia while Brown had 20 points in his return from a hamstring strain. Tyrese Maxey had 22 points and five assists, VJ Edgecombe had 12 points, seven assists, and seven rebounds, and Jabari Walker had 10 points and five rebounds. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers following the loss: Lack of size in the paint This one can be filed under the "Well, duh" category, but without Joel Embiid, who was sidelined with an illness, it was a struggle for the Sixers against a taller Trail Blazers team. Portland won the rebounding battle 49-33 led by Donovan Clingan's 18 rebounds and the Blazers were able to have a ton of success on the offensive end due to the size advantage. One has to give Walker credit for giving it his all. It was obvious that he was ready to battle and do what he had to do, but he can't help the size mismatch with Clingan and Co. in Portland. "I think the biggest challenge is just how much help you can provide," Walker said after the loss. "Sometimes when the guards get downhill, it makes you question whether you can help and then get back. So that’s always in your mind when a guy like that is on the floor." Brown's foul trouble Brown looked phenomenal to start the night as he scored 19 points on 8-for-10 shooting in the first half as Philadelphia was able to keep up with Portland. However, Brown picked up his fourth foul early in the third quarter and had to sit the rest of the third, returned in the fourth, and just could not find his rhythm again. He only scored one point on 0-for-4 shooting and he knocked down a free-throw in the second half for his only offensive contributions. The 5-time All-Star was able to give Philadelphia an offensive threat, but the foul trouble really slowed him after halftime as the Trail Blazers took control. "I wasn't too happy about it," Brown said. "It’s over with now. I think that affected the game. It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half. I sit the whole third quarter and coming back off injury, coming back from hamstring. Just my body didn't really feel the same after that." The 3-point discrepancy Another big issue was the 3-point difference for both teams. The Sixers shot 9-for-33 from deep while the Blazers knocked down 19 on 42 attempts on the night. That 30-point difference is tough to make up for anybody, but especially for a Sixers team that had to play small with Embiid sidelined. Philadelphia not only couldn't make up for the rebounding and paint differences, but it also couldn't figure out the 3-point line either. Afterward, coach Nick Nurse stated: Well, I think that first of all, they outplayed us. Their energy and just hustle in general was excellent throughout the game. But the big thing is the three-point shooting, I think. It's hard to lose by 10 on that particular stat. Ten makes, that's 30 points. That's hard to overcome unless you're going to beat them at the free throw line extensively, or else you're going to win the turnover battle extensively as well. But possession battle was pretty even. And then they make 10 more 3s than you. And it's too bad, too, because I think we go 0-for-4 with Jabari, Dean (Wade), KCP (Kentavious Caldwell-Pope). And I think other than one of those, they were all great shots. Maybe one of KCP's, he had to arc it a little higher over Clingan coming out at him. But other than that, I think they were really good shots. So, would have liked to defensive rebound a little bit better. We got our share of them, too. Second chance points weren't too big of a difference really, but the three-point shooting was.
