item.title: Kolo Toure: ‘De Bruyne didn’t want to leave City, McTominay has been a surprise’
item.description: Kolo Toure: ‘De Bruyne didn’t want to leave City, McTominay has been a surprise’ Former Manchester City defender and assistant coach Kolo Toure says that Kevin De Bruyne never wanted to leave the Premier League side and says that he will want to show the fans that he is still at the top of his game when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, and admits that Scott McTominay’s form in Serie A has been a surprise. The Ivorian, who served as an assistant to Pep Guardiola at City last season and was also part of Roberto Mancini’s Premier League winning squad in 2011-12, spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of the meeting between Napoli and Manchester City in the Champions League on Tuesday night. NEWCASTLE UPON TYNE, ENGLAND – JANUARY 13: Manchester City assistant manager Kolo Toure looks on during the Carabao Cup Semi Final First Leg match between Newcastle United and Manchester City at St James’ Park on January 13, 2026 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) Napoli head to the Etihad under pressure in the Champions League with just three points to their name from their first four matches of the competition in 2026-27, leaving them at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds. There will be returns to Manchester for a number of Napoli players, including Man City legend De Bruyne, as well as former Manchester United stars McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund, all expected to start on the night. Toure on Man City vs. Napoli, De Bruyne and McTominay Asked how he sees Tuesday night’s game going, Toure told La Gazzetta dello Sport: “City will try to control the game and crush Napoli, and I think Allegri will set up with a compact team, careful in defence but ready to explode on the counter-attack, which could be dangerous. City will have to avoid those.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 18: Jeremy Doku of Manchester City scores his team’s second goal past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic of Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD1 match between Manchester City and SSC Napoli at City of Manchester Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Asked what City can do to prevent being hit on the counter, Toure said: “Two ways. The first is to start by pressing opponents immediately after losing the ball. The second is to have players fast enough on the pitch to get back into defensive positions once the counter-attack starts.” Toure was asked for his thoughts on De Bruyne. The Belgian superstar is into the final year of his contract with Napoli and there have been reports that he could look to leave as early as January. “Kevin was one of the best players in the history of the Premier League,” said Toure. “He is an incredible player, but more than anything, a great person. For me, what counts in football is what you do on the pitch, but what you do off it is also extremely important. Kevin is a champion in that respect. DE BRUYNE, ITALY – NOVEMBE
item.content:encoded: Kolo Toure: ‘De Bruyne didn’t want to leave City, McTominay has been a surprise’ Former Manchester City defender and assistant coach Kolo Toure says that Kevin De Bruyne never wanted to leave the Premier League side and says that he will want to show the fans that he is still at the top of his game when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, and admits that Scott McTominay’s form in Serie A has been a surprise. The Ivorian, who served as an assistant to Pep Guardiola at City last season and was also part of Roberto Mancini’s Premier League winning squad in 2011-12, spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of the meeting between Napoli and Manchester City in the Champions League on Tuesday night. NEWCASTLE UPON TYNE, ENGLAND – JANUARY 13: Manchester City assistant manager Kolo Toure looks on during the Carabao Cup Semi Final First Leg match between Newcastle United and Manchester City at St James’ Park on January 13, 2026 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) Napoli head to the Etihad under pressure in the Champions League with just three points to their name from their first four matches of the competition in 2026-27, leaving them at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds. There will be returns to Manchester for a number of Napoli players, including Man City legend De Bruyne, as well as former Manchester United stars McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund, all expected to start on the night. Toure on Man City vs. Napoli, De Bruyne and McTominay Asked how he sees Tuesday night’s game going, Toure told La Gazzetta dello Sport: “City will try to control the game and crush Napoli, and I think Allegri will set up with a compact team, careful in defence but ready to explode on the counter-attack, which could be dangerous. City will have to avoid those.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 18: Jeremy Doku of Manchester City scores his team’s second goal past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic of Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD1 match between Manchester City and SSC Napoli at City of Manchester Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Asked what City can do to prevent being hit on the counter, Toure said: “Two ways. The first is to start by pressing opponents immediately after losing the ball. The second is to have players fast enough on the pitch to get back into defensive positions once the counter-attack starts.” Toure was asked for his thoughts on De Bruyne. The Belgian superstar is into the final year of his contract with Napoli and there have been reports that he could look to leave as early as January. “Kevin was one of the best players in the history of the Premier League,” said Toure. “He is an incredible player, but more than anything, a great person. For me, what counts in football is what you do on the pitch, but what you do off it is also extremely important. Kevin is a champion in that respect. DE BRUYNE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) “I know he didn’t want to leave City. I think he will want to show that he should have stated. I’m sure he wants to make a difference for Napoli, but also to show the fans who still love him that he’s still the top player he was at City.” Toure admitted that it has been a ‘surprise’ to see quite how much McTominay has kicked on since moving to Serie A. “Honestly, yes [it has been a surprise]. But I listened to a podcast that he was on not too long ago and it became clear to me that he is a fighter, and that he’s very strong and intelligent. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) “He’s always been good physically, but he didn’t show enough of his technical qualities in the Premier League. He’s pulled them out in Italy and has also added the finishing touches in the final third. For me, he will be Napoli’s key player.” Asked for his predictions for Man City’s player of the match, Toure replied: “Enzo Fernandez. He’s in great form and is making the difference in midfield. Just like Haaland in attack.” Toure was then asked where he thinks the differences lie between Man City under Pep Guardiola last season and City under Maresca in 2026-26. He replied: “When you change coach, especially one of Guardiola’s calibre, for me, the best there has ever been, it’s always a challenge. City have also lost key players like Bernardo Silva, like Rodri, the best midfielder in the role. And leaders like Stones and Ake. “I think City did a great job in bringing in strong players like Fernandez and Bouaddi. Maresca needs time, but I’m sure they’ll find a way.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 17: Enzo Maresca, Manager of Manchester City, looks on before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Ipswich Town at Etihad Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) Toure is not concerned by the recent form of Italy international goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. “Gigio is a fantastic person,” he said. Maybe he’s going through a tough period, but he’s an exemplary professional and knows exactly what he needs to do to return to his best level. And I’m sure he will because he’s one of the best goalkeepers in the world.”

item.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
item.description: LeBron James will make $15m a year from his deal with Polymarket. Photograph: Matt Slocum/AP When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Related: Victor Wembanyama said no to gambling money. In today’s NBA, that feels radical Giannis, Sampras, Mourinho, LeBron: these are all wealthy individuals with giant reputations to protect. What exactly is going on here? Surely whatever money is on offer from these platforms is functionally immaterial to these men’s bank balances; surely the predicticoin is not worth the cultural damage that comes from being associated with an industry that’s seen as a symptom of professional sport’s moral rot. Or is it? Is the money really too good to refuse? Has the contest for attention in modern sport and culture become so furious that even famed recluses like Sampr
item.content:encoded: LeBron James will make $15m a year from his deal with Polymarket. Photograph: Matt Slocum/AP When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Related: Victor Wembanyama said no to gambling money. In today’s NBA, that feels radical Giannis, Sampras, Mourinho, LeBron: these are all wealthy individuals with giant reputations to protect. What exactly is going on here? Surely whatever money is on offer from these platforms is functionally immaterial to these men’s bank balances; surely the predicticoin is not worth the cultural damage that comes from being associated with an industry that’s seen as a symptom of professional sport’s moral rot. Or is it? Is the money really too good to refuse? Has the contest for attention in modern sport and culture become so furious that even famed recluses like Sampras are suddenly gripped by a desperation to be maximally visible and “relevant”? Is the whole infrastructure of sport now so thoroughly poisoned by gambling and speculation thatthe stain that might once have come from taking money off such businesses has been cleaned? Perhaps it’s a bit of all three. Kalshi and Polymarket, ravenous for any shred of positive exposure and racing toward public offerings before the bottom falls out of the stock market, are deploying vast sums of money in a bewildering variety of directions to get on the American public’s good side. Every writer in US media today has heard stories of journalists being offered tens of thousands of dollars for even the most anodyne forms of engagement (replies, likes) with the online output of the prediction markets. Even for a billionaire like LeBron, a $15m annual pay packet is probably hard to resist. But it’s also important to put these grubby little partnerships between already-wealthy athletes and the prediction markets into their proper cultural context: the Kalshi dollars are raining down on the expensively polished heads of the sporting plutocrats at a time of collective obsession, not only in sports but across culture, with “getting this bread”. You only have to listen to Magic Johnson ( estimated net worth: $1.6bn) ruefully reflect on the time he turned down stock in Nike (“Five billion dollars it would have been worth today”) to understand that for the already obscenely wealthy, there is no greater loss than a lost opportunity for more wealth. This is an axiom of American success: once you are rich, it is important to get richer. In basketball, the rule of separation is paramount. Scoring is a game of space; to make room for a shot, a pass, a dribble, it’s critical that offensive players find ways to separate themselves from their defenders. In an increasingly unequal economy, especially one in which the AI doomers all assure us that there are only a few years of productive mass employment left before the machines swallow all the jobs, the need to find separation moves from a law of sport to a law of social self-preservation, and it’s hard not to detect the outlines of a basic instinct for financial survival in the otherwise unfathomable avarice guiding the decision of these wealthy sporting personalities to sell their souls to the prediction markets. If the economic apocalypse is nigh, hoarding wealth – from whatever quarter it comes – starts to look like common sense; it’s a way to guarantee a seat on the lifeboat, to stay an asset-owning winner in a society that will soon be awash with unsalaried and insolvent losers. Meanwhile, for those outside the 1%, economic uncertainty means that the embrace of “risk-on” thinking – and its corollary; the distortion of prudent household economic management into a series of risky, venture capital-style bets – has come to seem like a financial necessity. Going big on Kalshi and Polymarket now takes its place alongside crypto investing, borrowing on margin, and meme stock trading as a favored hosanna of the American mark. The siren call of the prediction markets increasingly makes social and economic sense for both ends of the income distribution. Amid a cost of living crisis, the ongoing stagnation in wages and the insulting weakness of the US social safety net , high-risk speculation is a last resort for those stuck in the lower percentiles, while for those at the top, embracing the prediction dollar is a riskless win. The sports themselves, of course, have done nothing to disincentive gambling’s well-heeled shills from pursuing their own greed and immorality to its logical ends. Only a few years after sports betting was legalized, professional sport in the US is now a full-time hostage of the gambling and prediction industries. Gambling odds and prediction percentages gum up the screen of every US sports broadcast, almost every league has a partnership with a prediction market (most recently the NBA announced a deal with both Kalshi and Polymarket), and the sheer density of branding in stadiums and sports media from the betting and prediction platforms has made it functionally impossible for fans to evade speculation’s cultural reach. The prediction markets have become normalized; they are now seen as an acceptable part of the furniture, a fact of everyday sporting life. In this environment, it’s no wonder the untroubled rich-guy endorsements have begun to flow. The Democrats’ outperformance in the recent midterm elections has raised expectations of a stiffer approach to federal regulation of the prediction platforms after two years in which the Trump-led White House enabled and encouraged their worst excesses. That seems, in truth, like a forlorn hope: already Kalshi has cut ties with Donald Trump Jr and moved to distance itself from the Trump administration, repositioning for a Democratic-controlled Congress. item.title: New Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino eyes summer raid on Borussia Dortmund for frustrated 17-year-old USMNT wonderkid
item.description: United States v Peru - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly eyeing a summer raid on Borussia Dortmund for frustrated 17-year-old USMNT wonderkid Mathis Albert. Having previously worked with the highly-rated attacker while coaching the United States, the Argentine could offer him a route to Old Trafford if his limited minutes in Germany continue. Pochettino monitors frustrated Dortmund teenager According to Sky Germany , Pochettino could push United to sign Albert amid his lack of regular action at Dortmund. The 17-year-old attacking talent has been restricted to just 128 minutes across three appearances this season, sparking dissatisfaction over his sporting situation. He was handed a rare outing on Saturday, coming off the bench in the 72nd minute of Dortmund's 1-0 win over Borussia Monchengladbach . Argentine admires young American attacker Pochettino knows Albert's qualities well, having nurtured the youngster early on and handed him his senior call-up during his spell as United States head coach. Following his recent appointment at Old Trafford , the connection between the two has gained fresh momentum as the Red Devils plan for the future. The report states that Pochettino remains a big admirer of his former international charge and believes "Albert needs to play" to fulfil his potential. Should the teenager's situation in the Bundesliga fail to improve over the coming months, the Argentine coach could offer him the chance to earn more regular first-team minutes in England. Teenager already broke USMNT record Widely regarded as one of Dortmund's brightest academy prospects, Albert is still waiting for a genuine senior breakthrough in Germany. Across all competitions, he has made four first-team appearances for BVB, with his only start to date coming in the first round of the DFB Cup back in early September. At international level, however, he has already collected five caps for the United States. On September 30, 2026, he netted in a 4-2 win over Chile at 17 years and 131 days old to become the USMNT's youngest-ever goalscorer in just his second outing, though Cavan Sullivan broke that mark four days later against Mexico aged 17 years and six days. Summer window could prove decisive A winter transfer is currently off the table, with the German outlet noting that Albert wants to see how the rest of the campaign unfolds first. He will closely monitor his playing time at Dortmund over the next few months before deciding on his next step. If his frustration persists, Pochettino and United are poised to make a concrete summer move.

item.title: ‘Ick,’ ‘That Body Language Says It All’ — Commanders Fans Take Issue With Ja’Marr Chase’s Assessment of Why Bengals Lost on MNF
item.description: ‘Ick,’ ‘That Body Language Says It All’ — Commanders Fans Take Issue With Ja’Marr Chase’s Assessment of Why Bengals Lost on MNF Ja’Marr Chase and the Cincinnati Bengals entered Monday’s game with a five-game winning streak and were looking to improve their 7-2 record. However, Washington produced a late comeback to secure the 22-20 win. The loss ended Cincinnati’s winning run and dropped the team to 7-3 this season. Chase had been enjoying a magnificent season heading into the MNF matchup, but the Commanders’ defense managed to keep the wide receiver largely quiet. Meanwhile, Chase’s reaction to the Bengals’ loss to the Commanders also earned him jabs from fans. Commanders Fans Question Ja’Marr Chase’s Confidence After Washington Silences Bengals Chase was coming off a phenomenal 231-yard outing against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 10. However, he finished against Washington with just five receptions for 31 yards on nine targets, without a touchdown, ranking No. 2 in PFN’s WR Impact Score with a grade of 96.1 through Week 11. Following the Bengals’ loss and his own underwhelming performance, Chase was asked about the most difficult aspect of coming away from a loss. “Losing when you know you’re better. That’s the worst.” Chase said , according to Mike Petraglia. Commanders fans used the chance to poke fun at Chase. “Ja’Marr Chase has never beaten the Washington Commanders in his entire career, idk what type of pedestal he thinks the Bengals are compared to the Commanders,” a fan said . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “0-2 btw… Higgins and Burrow 0-3 vs DC,” one said . “Whew.. that body language says it all,” one added . Washington’s defensive approach also played a significant role in limiting Cincinnati’s offensive production. The Commanders entered the game with one of the highest blitz rates in the NFL and continued to apply pressure to Joe Burrow throughout. The Commanders sacked Burrow three times, while the Bengals receiving duo of Chase and Tee Higgins combined for only seven catches for 74 yards. Commanders fans had reason to challenge Chase’s assessment because Cincinnati has now lost its last three meetings against Washington. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “ICKKKKK,” another said . “The Bengals ranked 2nd in EPA/play and success rate entering MNF. The marks they achieved on MNF would have the following ranks for the season: EPA/play – 17th, success rate – 28th. Perhaps the better team didn’t hit it’s usual standard against a defense missing three starter,” Grant Mitchell, host of the ‘Full Command Show,’ wrote . “You are 0-2 against us and Burrow is 0-3. Know your place, one added . The Bengals will now look to bounce back when they return home to face the New Orleans Saints in Week 12. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Tuesday ‘Dawg Bites Ain’t Got Time For That
item.description: ATHENS, GA - NOVEMBER 14: University of Georgia mascot UGA XI stands on the field during the college football game between the Missouri Tigers and the University of Georgia Bulldogs on November 14, 2026 at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to Tuesday, Bulldog fans! And the last Tuesday of the 2026 regular season. It has certainly flown by, but we’ve no time for reminiscing. Because once again, it is Hate Week. That of the Clean, Old-Fashioned variety. So while folks in College Station and Nashville try to relive the few moments of glory from the quickly ending season, and boards of directors in the bad Columbia and Red Stick fret over the weird December schedule affecting the coaching carousel, we UGA fans still have a lot of football to look forward to. And nothing has changed in the football offices, even this, the week of Thanksgiving. If you think the Dawgs are rounding into form and staying focused, that starts at the top. In Monday’s press conference, head coach Kirby Smart was peaking in his reponses to reporter’s questions. Curt a few times, deflecting a few more, praising his players whenever possible, and telling the assembled that they don’t know how a football program is run. In that vein, if you’ve seen social media posts or interweb headlines touting “What Kirby Smart Said About Glenn Schumann and the FSU Opening”, just breeze right on by. He said two things which can be summed up thusly: Schumann has done a wonderful job at UGA, and UGA is focused on Georgia Tech. Full stop. But you might not ignore the fact that both the school and Schumann himself have released statements on his offer and acceptance of steering the Seminole ship . Not much on the injury front either, as the only update on Center Drew Bobo was he hopes to have him available this week. It didn’t make much noise, but Earnest Greene III earned another SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week Award after having his way with the SC Gamecocks. Not quite as prestigious, the intrepid folks over at the Red & Black decided to put out another position group scorecard after the Pillaging of the Palmetto State. If the lowest grade is given to the wide receivers, you know it was a good night for the Bulldogs. There’s all kinds of other stories out there, like Lane Kiffin apologizing and throwing his roster under the bus, Kyle Whittingham continuing to coach for the buyout, UCLA reading the playbook on how to falsely reassure the CFP committee all is well, and another meeting next week to decide if LSU should remain in the Southeastern Conference. So, just another Tuesday. Safe travels to everyone out there, and safe food handling to all the others. Enjoy your Tuesday, and as always… GO ‘DAWGS!!!

It didn’t make much noise, but Earnest Greene III earned another SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week Award after having his way with the SC Gamecocks. Not quite as prestigious, the intrepid folks over at the Red & Black decided to put out another position group scorecard after the Pillaging of the Palmetto State. If the lowest grade is given to the wide receivers, you know it was a good night for the Bulldogs. There’s all kinds of other stories out there, like Lane Kiffin apologizing and throwing his roster under the bus, Kyle Whittingham continuing to coach for the buyout, UCLA reading the playbook on how to falsely reassure the CFP committee all is well, and another meeting next week to decide if LSU should remain in the Southeastern Conference. So, just another Tuesday. Safe travels to everyone out there, and safe food handling to all the others. Enjoy your Tuesday, and as always… GO ‘DAWGS!!!

item.title: MiLaysia Fulwiley Treated to Big Ovation From LSU Fans as Lady Tigers Star Hits 1,500 Career Points in Return After Arrest
item.description: MiLaysia Fulwiley ©IMAGO/Newscom World After piling up 17 steals and 11 blocks across her first four games, MiLaysia Fulwiley spent two outings on the sideline while unbeaten LSU rolled on without her. Nine days after her arrest in Baton Rouge, another question surrounded the senior guard’s return to the Pete Maravich Assembly Center against Belmont: How would LSU fans respond? Once she stepped back onto the floor, Monday night delivered far more than an ordinary return to the rotation. During LSU’s home matchup against Belmont on November 23, 2026, in Baton Rouge, Fulwiley checked in off the bench with 4:37 remaining in the first quarter and the Tigers already ahead 13–0. Covering the game courtside for the USA TODAY Network, reporter Cory Diaz documented the crowd’s response on X as MiLaysia Fulwiley made her first appearance in 10 days: “MiLaysia Fulwiley gets a big ovation from the #LSU fans here in the PMAC.” The warm welcome captured in Cory Diaz’s X post opened a productive night for Fulwiley, who returned from her two-game absence following a November 14 arrest to finish with 14 points, five steals, and 1,500 career points in LSU’s 103–45 win over Belmont. Later in the fourth quarter, with 1:35 remaining and LSU up 100–42, the arena video board honored the scoring milestone in a separate moment shared on X by reporter Andre Champagne. From the bench, MiLaysia Fulwiley waved and flashed a hand heart toward the cheering crowd while teammates celebrated around her. item.content:encoded: MiLaysia Fulwiley ©IMAGO/Newscom World After piling up 17 steals and 11 blocks across her first four games, MiLaysia Fulwiley spent two outings on the sideline while unbeaten LSU rolled on without her. Nine days after her arrest in Baton Rouge, another question surrounded the senior guard’s return to the Pete Maravich Assembly Center against Belmont: How would LSU fans respond? Once she stepped back onto the floor, Monday night delivered far more than an ordinary return to the rotation. During LSU’s home matchup against Belmont on November 23, 2026, in Baton Rouge, Fulwiley checked in off the bench with 4:37 remaining in the first quarter and the Tigers already ahead 13–0. Covering the game courtside for the USA TODAY Network, reporter Cory Diaz documented the crowd’s response on X as MiLaysia Fulwiley made her first appearance in 10 days: “MiLaysia Fulwiley gets a big ovation from the #LSU fans here in the PMAC.” The warm welcome captured in Cory Diaz’s X post opened a productive night for Fulwiley, who returned from her two-game absence following a November 14 arrest to finish with 14 points, five steals, and 1,500 career points in LSU’s 103–45 win over Belmont. Later in the fourth quarter, with 1:35 remaining and LSU up 100–42, the arena video board honored the scoring milestone in a separate moment shared on X by reporter Andre Champagne. From the bench, MiLaysia Fulwiley waved and flashed a hand heart toward the cheering crowd while teammates celebrated around her. A comeback moment and a historic milestone converge as MiLaysia Fulwiley reclaims her place on LSU's biggest stage. Subscribe for the latest on college basketball's most compelling stories. What MiLaysia Fulwiley’s Return Means for LSU After Two Games Out The night closed a turbulent stretch that began on November 14, when Fulwiley was arrested following a traffic-control encounter with police after LSU’s football game against Texas. Authorities initially booked her on two felony counts—aggravated battery and aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon—alongside three misdemeanor counts related to fleeing, resisting, and disobeying officers over alleged conduct during the stop. While the situation remained under review, she sat out LSU’s home wins over Troy on November 16 and Fairleigh Dickinson on November 19. Her path back opened on November 20, when East Baton Rouge Parish prosecutors dismissed both felony charges while referring the three misdemeanor counts to a pretrial diversion program rather than dismissing every matter outright. That same day, Fulwiley issued an apology through LSU acknowledging the night never should have happened and that her posts afterward made matters worse, apologizing to the officers, her family, and Tiger fans while focusing on earning back trust. Following a reported return to practice on November 21, LSU confirmed her availability ahead of Belmont . Coming off the bench after starting her first four games, Fulwiley needed less than a minute to make her presence felt by sinking a wing three-pointer on her first shot attempt. Across 17 minutes, she finished 6-of-13 from the field and 2-of-4 from beyond the arc while adding five steals, three blocks, three assists, and a rebound. Through five appearances in 2026–27, MiLaysia Fulwiley is now averaging 17.0 points, 4.4 steals, 4.0 assists, and 2.8 blocks. Her 14 points against Belmont carried added weight because they pushed her career scoring total to 1,500. Combining 904 points across two seasons at South Carolina, 511 points at LSU in 2025–26, and 71 points over her first four games this season—capped by 23 against Denver on November 13—she entered Monday sitting at 1,486. Remarkably, the milestone arrived almost exactly a year after LSU Athletics documented her crossing 1,000 career points with 18 points in a 112–49 win over Alcorn State on November 20, 2025. That scoring pace underscores why her reintegration matters so much to Kim Mulkey’s lineup. In her first season in Baton Rouge in 2025–26, MiLaysia Fulwiley led the Tigers with 511 points—averaging 14.6 per game—and captured her second straight SEC Sixth Woman of the Year award after winning a national championship at South Carolina in 2024. Bringing that proven perimeter scoring and defensive disruption back off the bench deepens an already dangerous roster. Still, Monday’s 58-point blowout was far from a one-player effort. LSU raced to a 22–0 opening run before Belmont scored with 17 seconds left in the first quarter, cruising to 7–0 while holding a sixth opponent in seven games under 50 points. Senior guard Mikaylah Williams paced the Tigers with 20 points and 10 assists, and all 11 LSU players who appeared reached the scoring column. Unbeaten LSU now heads away from Baton Rouge for the first time this season, facing Villanova on November 27 and NC State on November 28 at the neutral-site Fort Myers Tip-Off. Monday’s warm PMAC reception and 1,500-point milestone gave MiLaysia Fulwiley an immediate on-court reset in the rotation, while her remaining misdemeanor charges had been referred to diversion. item.title: Enzo Maresca has said Abdukodir Khusanov is better suited to centre-back than right-back as Manchester City weigh up their options ahead of the 2027 January transfer window.
item.description: Enzo Maresca has said Abdukodir Khusanov is better suited to centre-back than right-back as Manchester City weigh up their options ahead of the 2027 January transfer window. Right-back has been area of concern for Manchester City's leaky defence of late. More Videos Maresca has used Matheus Nunes as his first-choice right-back this season and the Portugal international is back in contention after an ankle problem kept him out of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Fulham . Abdukodir Khusanov started at right-back in Nunes' absence against Fulham, with Rodrigo Muniz getting the better of the Uzbekistan international for the opening goal before Elliot Anderson volleyed in a second-half equaliser. Maresca discusses Man City's right-back prospects ahead of Napoli test Speaking in a press conference ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League clash with Napoli, Maresca discussed his options at right-back following strong criticism aimed at the Blues' backline after a poor run of Premier League results. The Manchester City manager said: "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis] there, but also [Abdukodir] Khusa, that I think he can play there. For sure, it's much better - I'm trying to find the right balance. "If you ask me if Khusa [Khusanov] is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available. "But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good." City have been linked with Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman ahead of the January window, with sporting director Hugo Viana having overseen a major squad overhaul since Maresca's arrival in June. Freeman, a 22-year-old United States international who joined Villarreal from Orlando City in January, is said to be open to a move to the Etihad Stadium - and he can also play at centre-back. Maresca also pointed out on Monday that City had conceded seven goals from chances worth around three expected goals across their four-game winless run in the Premier League. It's just a matter of getting to know each other, says Maresca on Man City squad ahead of January window Maresca then explained that he is still getting to know his players, having witnessed a significant overhaul of the first-team dressing room since he replaced Pep Guardiola at the helm in June. "It's just a matter to know each other, I need to understand how is the idea one for these kind of games, the idea one for different kinds of games," the 46-year-old added. "I don't think it's just [the] midfield, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution. Again, it's for me part of the process because it's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. "It's not easy to all of sudden change. City have been linked with Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman ahead of the January window, with sporting director Hugo Viana having overseen a major squad overhaul since Maresca's arrival in June. Maresca also pointed out on Monday that City had conceded seven goals from chances worth around three expected goals across their four-game winless run in the Premier League. It's just a matter of getting to know each other, says Maresca on Man City squad ahead of January window Maresca then explained that he is still getting to know his players, having witnessed a significant overhaul of the first-team dressing room since he replaced Pep Guardiola at the helm in June. "It's just a matter to know each other, I need to understand how is the idea one for these kind of games, the idea one for different kinds of games," the 46-year-old added. "I don't think it's just [the] midfield, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution. Again, it's for me part of the process because it's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. "It's not easy to all of sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs." Manchester City have lacked a specialist right-back since Kyle Walker left for AC Milan in January 2025, and Nunes has made the position his own despite being a natural central midfielder, with the club reported to be close to agreeing a new contract amid interest from Real Madrid . Nunes was also partly at fault for Yasin Ayari's winner in the 1-0 defeat to Brighton last month, whilst Marc Guehi's loose touch led to Nicolas Jackson's opener at Villa Park a week earlier. Liam Delap's second goal in the 3-1 defeat at the City Ground came after the Forest striker flicked the ball past Anderson and Nunes before exchanging passes with Morgan Gibbs-White and finding the far post. Rico Lewis, who turned 22 last week, has filled in at right-back since breaking into the senior squad under Guardiola in 2022, but has said he would prefer to play in midfield , where he feels he can best contribute goals and assists for the team. City go into Tuesday's game against Napoli seventh of 36 in the Champions League league phase, with a top-eight finish guaranteeing direct qualification for the round of 16 and avoiding a February play-off.

item.title: Relief for Arsenal as Raya has not suffered a serious injury
item.description: Relief for Arsenal as Raya has not suffered a serious injury Arsenal have received a major boost after David Raya’s injury proved less serious than initially feared, with the goalkeeper potentially returning to action this weekend. The Spaniard was forced off against Newcastle United after suffering a suspected shoulder injury , leaving the club concerned about his availability for upcoming matches. Raya appeared to be in considerable discomfort following the incident and did not look comfortable as he made his way off the pitch. His reaction immediately raised concerns among Arsenal supporters, who feared the goalkeeper could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The club arranged for him to undergo scans after the match to establish the extent of the problem. Fortunately, the results did not reveal any serious damage, giving Arsenal encouragement that their first-choice goalkeeper could return much sooner than expected. Arteta provides encouraging injury update Raya is one of Arsenal’s most important players and has established himself as one of the leading goalkeepers in world football. Losing him for an extended period would have been a significant setback for Mikel Arteta’s side as they look to build on their success from last season. However, the latest assessment suggests the situation is not as concerning as it initially appeared. Raya will miss the Borussia Dortmund match, but there is now hope that he could be available again at the weekend. Speaking to Arsenal Media ahead of the Champions League fixture, Arteta provided an update on the goalkeeper’s condition and explained why the initial reaction had been worrying. He said: “He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. “With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than we expected. When you look at the action, it doesn’t seem to be much on it, but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.” (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Arsenal hope Raya returns quickly The Gunners will continue monitoring Raya before deciding when he can return. His availability would be a welcome boost, particularly with important fixtures approaching. Although Arsenal must manage without him against Dortmund, Arteta will be encouraged by the progress so far. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: ‘One of us’ – NFL fans praise Pat McAfee after hilarious reaction to Jason Kelce on MNF
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images ESPN’s Monday Night Football coverage has taken a lot of criticism this season, with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman’s saga being one of the big talking points. However, ESPN’s pre-game show and alt cast, including the controversial Pat McAfee, have also proven incredibly divisive. Despite a lot of fans having vented their frustrations with McAfee throughout the season, a lot of people loved what they saw him doing during this week’s show. Jason Kelce has also split the opinions of the viewers on ESPN, which left many fans on Monday night enjoying McAfee not paying any attention at all to the former Philadelphia Eagles centre. NFL fans provide rare praise towards Pat McAfee during Monday Night Football McAfee has been pushed considerably by ESPN over a number of different programmes, with the former Indianapolis Colts punter being made to earn every cent he is being paid by the network. ‘Pat McAfee isn’t even listening to Jason Kelce. One of us!’ one fan said on X during the pre-game show on Monday Night Football. Another fan replied: ‘And why would u? Jason Kelce just commented that Jayden Daniels has been so flawless in two-minute & end-of-game scenarios this season.’ It is rare to see McAfee earn the praise of the viewers, with many still feeling as if he is being given way too much airtime by ESPN. Alongside his own show during the week, McAfee is also presenting College Gameday and the Monday Night Football alt cast. ‘For 2027, ESPN should make its MNF broadcasters Joe Buck and Pat McAfee,’ said another NFL fan. McAfee has been known for being incredibly charitable, and alongside the NFL, he is now giving away Super Bowl tickets in a pre-game kickoff catch game. This is a feature which has also gone down extremely well with viewers on ESPN. ‘Don’t love his show, but Pat McAfee is changing folks’ lives weekly. I do appreciate that,’ one fan said on X. McAfee also made a $25,000 donation to The GR8 Chase charity ahead of kickoff as a result of the kickoff catch competition, which provided the fan with tickets to the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium. ‘Pat McAfee gives away MILLIONS to charity,’ replied another. NFL fans provide rare praise towards Pat McAfee during Monday Night Football McAfee has been pushed considerably by ESPN over a number of different programmes, with the former Indianapolis Colts punter being made to earn every cent he is being paid by the network. ‘Pat McAfee isn’t even listening to Jason Kelce. One of us!’ one fan said on X during the pre-game show on Monday Night Football. Another fan replied: ‘And why would u? Jason Kelce just commented that Jayden Daniels has been so flawless in two-minute & end-of-game scenarios this season.’ It is rare to see McAfee earn the praise of the viewers, with many still feeling as if he is being given way too much airtime by ESPN. Alongside his own show during the week, McAfee is also presenting College Gameday and the Monday Night Football alt cast. ‘For 2027, ESPN should make its MNF broadcasters Joe Buck and Pat McAfee,’ said another NFL fan. McAfee has been known for being incredibly charitable, and alongside the NFL, he is now giving away Super Bowl tickets in a pre-game kickoff catch game. This is a feature which has also gone down extremely well with viewers on ESPN. ‘Don’t love his show, but Pat McAfee is changing folks’ lives weekly. I do appreciate that,’ one fan said on X. McAfee also made a $25,000 donation to The GR8 Chase charity ahead of kickoff as a result of the kickoff catch competition, which provided the fan with tickets to the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium. ‘Pat McAfee gives away MILLIONS to charity,’ replied another. item.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
item.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last-16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund
item.description: Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League , with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut . But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager. Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match. Continue reading...

item.title: De Bruyne’s Napoli return will remind Manchester City what they are missing
item.description: Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times. Kevin De Bruyne will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday, evoking the greatest period of Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge when they won four straight Premier League titles and the Champions League . In Europe, things are comfortable for Enzo Maresca, with three wins from four, but they have collected a solitary point from 12 domestically recently. They are struggling to score and conceding too easily at the back, leading the Italian to experiment in his attempts to find solutions. Continue reading...

item.title: Lewis-Potter double and Janelt stunner ease Brentford past 10-man Everton
item.description: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances. Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out. Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite Galatasaray surface
item.description: ‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”. Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray. Continue reading...

item.title: PSG had the best attack in Europe but Doué and Kvaratskhelia injuries will test Luis Enrique
item.description: Désiré Doué sustained an ACL injury in PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice and joins Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the treatment table By Get French Football News Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”. Since arriving at Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, only three players have spent more than 100 days on the sideline – Nuno Mendes, Lucas Hernandez and Presnel Kimpembe – and only Mendes is an important first-team player. But for the remainder of the season, or at least the vast majority of it, Luis Enrique must do without two of his stars: Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Doué arrived in Nice on Saturday evening already bearing scars. The PSG forward wore a mouth guard after Davide Frattesi had dislodged one of his front teeth with a stray arm during France’s defeat by Italy during the international break. Continue reading...

item.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
item.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . item.title: Jamal Musiala controversy the nadir of Bayern Munich’s turbulent week
item.description: German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. Continue reading...

With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. Continue reading...

item.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
item.description: Management team were in line for huge payouts Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century. Continue reading...

item.description: We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a shock 3-1 victory away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” Tom Garry Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
item.description: Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit. “Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
item.description: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...
